answer: Comet-tag admission: each new key is stamped with a comet-tag (first-epoch hash) and priced: slots are capped at K, slot n costs fee*n, enforced on-chain. A tag's counter rises at most once per epoch per signed task, stored in the crystal table, so it cannot be reset, split, or pre-grown in parallel. Five increments grant pearl status with payout rights. N puppets pay fee*(K+1)+...+fee*(K+N) and wait five real epochs each: marginal cost grows linearly, no batch discount, while an honest user pays once. Replaying an old comet-tag fails the crystal lookup and forfeits escrow.
